question: Does a lagged historical airport traffic profile add predictive value beyond calendar and weather?
scope: All 100 major U.S. airports assessed independently; reporting-carrier domestic scheduled airport events only
historicalTrafficSource: Existing pre-weather-filter BTS two-hour aggregates, including cancelled flights and records with unknown delay outcomes
profileRule: At the start of each target local month, subtract 24 hours and 120 days; use only full source months ending before that date, within the preceding 12 calendar months. Freeze this profile for the target month at all horizons. Average counts by local weekday and two-hour block, including zero-count blocks on eligible source dates; do not treat missing source months as zero.
releaseCaveat: A conservative assumed release lag, not reconstructed BTS release vintages. Source files are final-vintage. This remains a retrospective exploratory experiment.
learner: Fixed airport-local regularized logistic heads, with the existing v3 regularization and separate probability and uncertainty calibration for every variant. Same eligible rows within each airport/direction/horizon comparison.
primaryMetric: Paired reduction in disruption Brier score: weatherTraffic versus weather
uncertainty: 1000 paired resamples of three-day calendar blocks; approximate BH correction across tested airport/direction/horizon slices separately by evaluation period. Aggregate direction/horizon intervals share sampled calendar blocks across airports.
selection: No tuning after inspecting test outcomes; no automatic model promotion. Local experiment comparators are not the retained pooled production models at the original 25 airports. Reduced training dates and eligibility prevent a direct before/after comparison with production.
budget: No downloads, paid API calls, or AWS jobs; use existing local data and two CPU threads. Leave production model, snapshots, and AWS budget controls unchanged.
